analysis: In all 34 commutative operations 0 is absorbing (no L, R options) or an identity (L and R); no simple closed form for the chaotic ones (tested candidates a^b^ab, (a^1)(b^1)^1, ab, ...). Of the diagonals and rows 1-3 looked up, 88 sequences have no OEIS match (e.g. the diagonal 0, 2, 1, 5, 7, 4, 3, 16, ... of L+R+D[x^y^z]); maximal values grow roughly quadratically (bounded by (a+1)(b+1) - 1). One match (L+R+D[x^y] diagonal 0, 2, 1, 1, 1, ... vs A137993) is a coincidence of an almost constant sequence.
assumptions: tables for a, b < 96; OEIS lookups cached in cache/oeis; constant, identity-like and arithmetic-progression sequences are not looked up
falsification: A commutative operation in which 0 is neither absorbing nor an identity, or a diagonal without OEIS match.
